description:
FILED s421 (Fable review of s420; found by the #414 probes).  PRE-EXISTING:
identical output at 47e0750 (pre-s420) and at s420 — not a regression.

    my @x=(10,20,30); my $r=\@x; my $h={a=>[5,6], b=>9}; my @i=(0,1,2);
    print "$$r[1]\n";          # perl 20        PCL ARRAY(0x1)[1]
    print "x $$r[1] y\n";      # perl x 20 y    PCL x ARRAY(0x1)[1] y
    print "$$h{b}\n";          # perl 9         PCL HASH(0x2){b}
    print "${$r}[1]\n";        # perl 20        PCL ARRAY(0x1)[1]
    print "@$r[0,1]\n";        # perl 10 20     PCL 10 20 30[0,1]
    print "@{$r}[1]\n";        # perl 20        PCL 10 20 30[1]
    print "$$h{a}[1]\n";       # perl 6         PCL HASH(0x2){a}[1]
    print "${$h}{a}[0]\n";     # perl 5         PCL HASH(0x2){a}[0]
    # these WORK: "$r->[$i[2]]", "@$r", "$x[$i[0]]" (#414), "$x[$h{k}]"

Emission for `"$$r[1]"`: (p-string-concat (p-cast-$ $r) "[1]") — the deref
is interpolated as a bare scalar deref and the subscript is left in the
literal.  perl's rule: inside a string, `$$name[` / `$$name{` / `${$name}[` /
`@$name[` / `@{$name}[` continue into the subscript exactly like `$name[`.

CORPUS COST (measured s421, dq-strings containing `$$NAME[` or `$$NAME{`):
perl-tests 0, lib/ 0, cpan-tests/modules 2 (both inside Carp.pm's eval TEXT),
perl's t/ 8 (mro/package_aliases*.t — the TAP DESCRIPTION strings, i.e. the
join keys, in XDIFF rows-unstable files).  So the measured cost is near
zero — but `"$$self{name}"` is a common pre-5.6 CPAN idiom, so the cost
outside the corpora is higher than the corpora say.

FIX SHAPE: Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm — the deref-variable path
(`$$name`, `${$name}`, `@$name`, `@{$name}`) must hand off to the SAME
subscript-chain continuation the plain `$name[` / `$name{` path uses (rule
11: one path, not a copy) — or land with #388's InterpScan consumer-3 port,
which replaces that scanner.  Acceptance: the table above vs perl, plus the
inverse guards `"$$r"`, `"@$r"`, `"$$r\[1]"` (escaped bracket stays literal),
and the email shapes `"$$r [1]"` / `"$$r@x"` — probe each vs perl before
asserting.  Sibling: #422 item 1 (`"@{^CAPTURE}"`), same file.

DONE s426 (Opus), as part of #388 consumer 3 â the port IS the fix, so the
s366 escape hatch was NOT taken.  Two halves, because the shape has two:

(a) THE SCANNER SIDE.  parse_interpolated_variable is a Pl::InterpScan
    scan_one dispatcher now; the event carries the subscript CHAIN, so a
    deref or braced-expression base continues into it and the whole
    reference is compiled from its own SOURCE TEXT through the ordinary
    expression pipeline.  Two scanner facts were probed and added while
    wiring: a braced EXPRESSION does not close the reference (a braced NAME
    does) and `@{^NAME}` is a magic array (that is #422.1).  Corpus reach of
    the port alone: 0 of 111 files â emission-identical.

(b) THE EMITTER SIDE, which the task did not know was there.  With the
    subscript finally reaching the parser, `"@$r[0,1]"` produced
    (p-aslice $r 0 1) and printed nothing: a slice whose CONTAINER is a
    SCALAR is a slice THROUGH A REFERENCE, and all four slice emitters
    handed the raw box to the slice runtime, which indexed the REFERENCE.
    That is a PRE-EXISTING silent-wrong in ORDINARY CODE, not only in
    strings â probed vs perl 5.40.3:
        my $ao=[7,8,9];  @$ao[1]        # 8      (right, by luck: one box layer)
        my $r=\@named;   @$r[0,1]       # ""     perl "10 20"   SILENT WRONG
        my $hr=\%named;  @$hr{'a','b'}  # DIED   perl "HA HB"
                         %$hr{'a'}      # DIED   perl "a=HA"
                         @$r[0,1]=(1,2) # no-op  perl assigns   SILENT WRONG
                         delete @$hr{'a'} # DIED perl "HA"
    Fix: one helper, _slice_container_form (Pl/ExprToCL.pm), used by
    gen_array_slice_form, gen_hash_slice_form, gen_kv_hash_slice_form,
    gen_kv_array_slice_form and _elem_container_key's slice arm â cast the
    container with p-cast-@ / p-cast-% unless the child node is a bare
    Symbol/Magic naming the aggregate.  It replaced gen_kv_array_slice_form's
    `(unbox $r)`, which was the same rule written shape-blind (right for a
    single-boxed anon ref, one layer short of \@named).

ACCEPTANCE MET: all 56 rows of the s426 ten-shape probe identical to perl
(the task's own table, the inverse guards `"$$r"` `"@$r"` `"$$r\[1]"`
`"$$r [1]"` `"$$r@x"`, and the #390/#414 nested-subscript set), plus 18
rows of the slice family in ordinary code.  Guards:
Pl/t/interp-chained-subscript-01.t rows 11 and 12.
title: "$$r[1]" / "$$h{k}" / "${$r}[i]" / "@$r[...]" / "@{$r}[i]" — a DEREF spelling with a trailing subscript INSIDE a dq string interpolates the deref and leaves the subscript as literal text (SILENT WRONG)
